title: An octopus has 3 hearts and blue blood!
question: Did you know octopuses have three hearts and blue blood?
answer: An octopus has three hearts, and its blood is blue when it carries oxygen, because it has copper in it.

visual.what: A friendly cartoon octopus floats in a bright blue sea, with three small glowing hearts shown on its round body and a drop of blue blood beside it.

parts.text: Did you know an octopus has three hearts and blue blood?

visual.what: A simple octopus body. Two small hearts sit next to two feathery gills, each with an arrow of blood going to the gill.

parts.text: Three hearts? I only have one!
Two hearts send blood to the gills. Gills are how an octopus breathes under water.

visual.what: The same octopus. The big third heart in the middle sends arrows of blood out to all eight arms and the head.

parts.text: The third heart pumps blood to the rest of the body.
Two hearts for the gills, one for everything else!

visual.what: Split picture. On the left, a child with a red blood drop marked with a small iron nail. On the right, an octopus with a blue blood drop marked with a copper coin.

parts.text: Our blood has iron in it, so it looks red.
Its blood has copper in it.

visual.what: A close-up of an octopus blood vessel. Tiny round oxygen bubbles join copper dots, and the liquid turns bright blue.

parts.text: When the copper holds oxygen, the blood turns blue.
Blue blood, like a sea superhero!

visual.what: Huy and Mai wave happily next to a smiling octopus showing three hearts, with a Follow button popping up.

parts.text: Three hearts and blue blood. What a wow animal!
Follow Ask Huy for more wow facts!

facts.claim: Octopuses have three hearts. Two pump blood to the gills and the third pumps it to the rest of the body.
Hemocyanin is a protein that carries oxygen in some animals, including cephalopods such as octopuses. It contains two copper atoms.
Oxygen turns hemocyanin from colorless to blue.
Human blood is red because of hemoglobin, and blood is bright red when its hemoglobin carries oxygen. Hemoglobin holds iron.
